title: Impact of PHP vulnerabilities on Wikimedia tools and services
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation is currently preparing for two critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language that underpins much of what we operate today. These vulnerabilities are severe and require affected website owners to take immediate action. This issue is not specific to the Wikimedia Foundation, but affects any website running PHP. This is a significant internet security vulnerability that many organizations are responding to right now.

We are working to avoid downtime for our wikis, but we have deliberately taken many of our supporting services offline until they can be safely patched.

title: IMILI and Wikimedia Nigeria Partner to Advance Media and Information Literacy, Information Integrity, and Open Knowledge in Nigeria
content:
How a connection facilitated by the Wikimedia Foundation’s Advocacy team opened the door to a partnership with the International Media and Information Literacy Institute (IMILI), a UNESCO Category 2 Institute with an international mandate.

Sometimes, an important partnership begins with a simple introduction.

For Wikimedia UG Nigeria, that introduction came through Costanza Caniglia of the Wikimedia Foundation’s Advocacy team. What began as an opportunity to connect with a contact within the United Nations system gradually grew into a series of institutional engagements, new relationships, and conversations about how the Wikimedia Movement could contribute to broader efforts to improve information literacy and access to knowledge.

Those conversations eventually led to a major milestone.

title: Lessons from Accra: Rossouw van Rooyen’s take on what the first Language Diversity Conference meant for Africa’s languages
content:
Early in the first Language Diversity Conference, Rossouw van Rooyen thought about a quote he had first heard eight years earlier.

At Wikimania 2018 in Cape Town, Daniel Bögre Udell of Wikitongues quoted Richard Henry Pratt. Pratt founded the Carlisle Indian Industrial School, a notorious US boarding school for Native American children, and summed up its mission as “kill the Indian in him, and save the man”. Seeing Daniel again in Accra set the tone for Rossouw’s weekend.

“There are languages being eradicated, there are languages being suppressed all over the world which we need to save,” he says. He adds that the work is “going to be a never-ending quest.”

The conference ran in Accra, Ghana, from 2 to 4 October 2026. It was hosted by the Wikimedia Language Diversity Hub, Wikitongues and Wikimedia UK, with the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group. 82 languages were represented in the room.

title: Strengthening Language Communities: My Experience at the Language Diversity Conference
content:
The Language Diversity Conference took place from October 2nd to 4th under the inspiring theme “Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Knowledge Movement.” The event brought together language activists, Wikimedians, and open knowledge advocates from across the globe, creating a space to share strategies, celebrate linguistic diversity, and tackle the ongoing content divide facing indigenous languages.

I was honored to present a session titled “Unlocking the Voice: Advocacy for Indigenous Language Digitization.” My presentation focused on moving beyond theoretical language preservation to provide a practical, low-barrier roadmap for local communities.

I introduced a simple framework designed for language advocates:

1. Record: Utilizing accessible, everyday technology such as smartphones and open tools like Lingua Libre to capture oral histories, proverbs, and vocabulary directly from native speakers.

2. Respect: Ensuring full community consent, respecting cultural protocols, and treating community elders as co-creators rather than data sources.

title: WikiScholar 2027: bringing young readers back to Wikipedia in the age of AI
content:
Registration for WikiScholar 2027 opened on 18 October 2026. WikiScholar is a free, annual knowledge competition for students in Grades 6–10 across Bangladesh, and its entire syllabus is a reading list of Bangla Wikipedia articles.

The competition is organised by Wikimedia Bangladesh, with support from a leading corporation in Bangladesh and the Wikimedia Foundation. Students can register at registration.wikischolar.bd until 12 December 2026.

In 2026 we ran WikiScholar as a pilot in 18 schools across Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions, reaching more than 10,000 students. This year it goes nationwide.

The country’s 64 districts are grouped into six regions, each named after a river: Padma, Teesta, Karnaphuli, Surma, Rupsha and Jamuna. Every student competes in the regional round for their own region.

There are three rounds: one online, then two held in person. All dates are provisional.

The online test has 60 multiple-choice questions in 35 minutes. Questions match the board exams in difficulty, mixing knowledge-based and analytical questions. A written question may be added, but it is marked only to break ties.

title: Event brings together experts and Wikimedians to discuss internet governance in Brazil
content: Brazil is widely recognized as having one of the populations that spends the most amount of time online, averaging over 115 hours of connectivity per week. Discussing the regulation of social media, online platforms, and artificial intelligence, technologies that increasingly shape the daily lives of Brazilians, is essential. This is particularly relevant within the context of Wikimedia Brasil’s Theory of Change (2024), which advocates for the organization to take a more active role in advocacy for broad, democratic digital rights, maintaining a stance of intentionality in defending free, collaborative projects that serve the public interest.

title: The Train the Trainers Nigeria, North-West 2025; Kano State
content: The Train the Trainers (TTT) programme is an initiative of the Wikimedia User Group Nigeria (WUGN) aimed at equipping Wikimedians with the skills and knowledge needed to train others to contribute effectively to Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. Previous editions have been organised across different regions of Nigeria, including North-Central, South-East, and North-East, helping to expand participation in the Wikimedia movement, develop new generations of editors, and improve content coverage across Wikimedia platforms. Building on these efforts, the Train the Trainers North West Nigeria 2025 was organised to strengthen community leadership, promote knowledge sharing, and support the sustainable growth of Wikimedia communities across the region.

content:

Updates for editors

  • To measure the impact of incorporating some community-requested features on logged-out reader retention, a test for Image Carousel will be pushed to logged-out readers. With the Image Carousel feature, readers browse community-uploaded images, selected by editors as relevant to specific articles. The test starts on November 20.
  • An experimental notice will be pushed to 0.5% of logged-out mobile readers who come to English Wikipedia from Google, asking them to add Wikipedia as a Google Preferred Source. The test is to see if this notice increases reader retention and encourages people who use Google Search to visit Wikipedia more often. It will run from October 15–29 and will be assessed for its impact on retention and referrals.

title: Building Bridges between Bangladesh-China through Wikimedia
content:
How university life in Changsha became an opportunity to bring language, culture, and free knowledge together.

When I moved to Changsha, China to study Electrical Engineering and Automation at Changsha University of Science and Technology (CSUST), I was also thinking of a different kind of infrastructure: the infrastructure of knowledge, language and cultural representation on the internet.

As a polyglot Bengali and Sylheti-speaking student, far away from Bangladesh, the Wikimedia projects were a way to stay connected to my language and be part of a global movement for free knowledge. In 2019, that interest began to take shape beyond individual edits, through in-person gatherings that brought Bangla Wikipedia contributors and Chinese Wikimedians together. In 2020, I was featured by Changsha Evening News for my involvement in promoting cultural exchange between Bangladesh and China as a cultural ambassador.

title: Beyond Wikipedia: Training Editors with Wikimedia Nigeria, Rivers Network
content:
When you hear Wikipedia, do you ever stop to think about the other Wikimedia projects?

That was the idea behind Beyond Wikipedia: Exploring the Wikimedia Projects, a training series organised by Wikimedia Nigeria,Rivers Network, where different trainers took participants through different Wikimedia projects, including Diff, Wikiquote, Wikiversity, Wikimedia Commons, Wikisource, and Wikipedia. I was one of the trainers, and I handled the Wikipedia session.

Nubel Bariloe, the Vice President of the Network, reached out to invite me to be one of the trainers. I was like, why not? I appreciated how he handled the invitation. He sent a formal invitation and followed up with me about the date. I would tell him I remembered. One thing I particularly appreciated was his communication. He was consistent throughout the process, and I give him kudos for that.
snippet: When you hear Wikipedia, do you ever stop to think about the other Wikimedia projects?
creator: Aderiqueza

title: Bridges Built: EduWiki Hub and ESEAP Hub Strengthen Access to Wikimedia Education
content:
What can happen when a global education-focused community and a regional Wikimedia hub connect their existing work?

For the EduWiki Hub and the Wikimedia East, Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ESEAP) Hub, the answer has been a practical partnership focused on making Wikimedia education opportunities more accessible, visible, and relevant to communities across the ESEAP region.

The collaboration has grown around a shared principle: accessibility and inclusivity. Rather than creating a separate program, the two hubs have connected existing activities, resources, and community networks to help more people participate.

One of the most concrete areas of collaboration has been language access. Through the ESEAP Hub’s Community Translator Program, EduWiki Hub activities including Knowledge Showcases, Workshops, and the Newcomer’s Starter Kit orientation have received interpretation support, including Indonesian and Chinese interpretation.
snippet: What can happen when a global education-focused community and a regional Wikimedia hub connect their existing work?
creator: RMaliqi EdWH

title: Making Northern Nigerian Women Visible through Wikimedia: The Wikimedia4EliteWomen Campaign
content: Many educated and accomplished women from Northern Nigeria have made significant contributions to education, research, healthcare, entrepreneurship, public service, and community development. Yet, their stories and achievements remain underrepresented in the digital knowledge space. The Wikimedia4EliteWomen Awareness Campaign 2026 was created to address this gap by raising awareness, encouraging participation in Wikimedia projects, and promoting the documentation of women’s contributions for a global audience.Running from 30th June to 10th August 2026, the campaign brought together people interested in gender equity, free knowledge, and the representation of women whose achievements deserve wider recognition. Through community engagement, onboarding, and practical training, the initiative encouraged participants to become active contributors to the Wikimedia movement.

title: Representation, Visibility, and Contact Zones: the North America Hub at WikiConference North America 2026
content:
Last month, Wikimedians from across the continent gathered in beautiful Edmonton, Alberta for WikiConference North America (WCNA) 2026—an opportunity to share projects, learn from one another, and think collectively about what it means to build and sustain the knowledge commons. For those of us working on the Wikimedia North America Hub, it was also a wonderful chance to meet so many community members in person and listen to the extraordinary work already happening across our region.

Throughout the conference, one theme surfaced repeatedly: representation is not simply a matter of adding more information. It requires attention to whose knowledge becomes visible, who gets to participate in creating it, and what structures shape that participation.

title: Indic MediaWiki Developers User Group WikiConference India 2026 Report
content:
WikiConference India 2026 was the fourth edition of the national conference. It was held in Kochi, Kerala, from 4–6 September 2026 and hosted by the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, in collaboration with the Wikimedians of Kerala User Group. The conference brought together Wikimedians, developers, researchers, educators, community organisers and other contributors, with more than 220 participants from India and other countries. The conference was organised around the theme “Reimagining the Knowledge Commons: Community Leadership in an Evolving Wikimedia Ecosystem.”

Indic MediaWiki Developers User Group (IMDUG) works to provide technical support to Indic Wikimedia projects and communities through technical capacity-building activities. For the IMDUG, WCI 2026 provided an opportunity to engage directly with Wikimedia editor communities and better understand the technical challenges they face in their day-to-day workflows.
